column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/pleme-ops.yml
# TAB-separated: <name>
# WHAT THIS PINS. pleme-ops is a TIER-2 composer: 17 sibling jobs, no `needs`,
# no status functions, each gated on one equality against `inputs.target`. The
# whole contract is a dispatch table, so the whole contract is: exactly one arm
# selects, and it is the arm named. Every row therefore asserts the FULL skip
# set rather than only the arm under test — a dispatcher's characteristic
# defect is a copy-pasted condition (`data-stack: if: inputs.target ==
# 'cd-stack'`), which a partial row would catch once and a full row catches
# from both sides. 272 skip assertions is the price of that; it is paid by a
# generator, not by hand.
# THE BOUNDARY ROW IS `empty-target`. `target` is `required: true`, so a caller
# cannot omit it — but pleme.yml passes it through by interpolation, and an
# interpolation that resolves to nothing yields the empty string, not an error.
# Every arm then compares false, all 17 jobs skip, and the composer reports
# SUCCESS having dispatched nothing. That is the graphql-synthesizer shape
# exactly: a green tick over an empty selection. It is asserted here so a
# no-op dispatch is a written-down expectation instead of an indistinguishable
# one. `unknown-target` is its sibling — a live-but-unrecognised value, which
# is what a renamed leaf or a stale caller sends, and which this workflow
# deliberately has NO catch-all for.
# NO TOGGLE ROWS: the workflow has exactly one input and no boolean gate, so
# there is no toggle to prove load-bearing.
# SCOPE LIMIT, stated so nobody reads more into a green run than it carries:
# this asserts which `uses:` DISPATCHES select. The linter does not model
# reusable-workflow `with:` propagation into a called workflow's own
# conditions, so a green row proves the leaf was invoked, never that the leaf's
# own jobs ran. Each leaf carries (or needs) its own table.
# ROWS THAT TRIGGER A SIDE EFFECT downstream — each appears once as do-it and
# 18 times as don't-do-it, which is the intended posture: this composer fires
# one and only one of them per call.
#   crates-publish: publishes crates to crates.io
#   esteira-rio-bump: pushes a bump commit
#   esteira-rio-release: cuts + pushes a release
#   mac-autobump-release: bumps + publishes a mac artifact
#   observability-deploy: deploys to a live observability stack
#   reusable-flakehub: publishes a flake to FlakeHub
#   super-cache-ci-build: pushes build artifacts to the cache
t-ai-stack
t-auto-release-verify
t-cd-stack
t-comment-command-dispatch
t-container-stack
t-crates-publish
t-cse-audit
t-data-stack
t-esteira-rio-bump
t-esteira-rio-release
t-ios-game-ci
t-mac-autobump-release
t-observability-deploy
t-reusable-flakehub
t-security-gate
t-super-cache-ci-build
t-web3-stack
# A live value matching no arm. No catch-all exists, and that is the design:
# an unrecognised target must dispatch NOTHING rather than guess an arm.
unknown-target
# Detect-ran-but-produced-nothing. An upstream interpolation that resolved to
# empty is indistinguishable from a successful dispatch at the caller; here it
# is pinned as a total no-op.
empty-target
